459: theorem dimH_univ_pi_fin (n : ℕ) : dimH (univ : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) = n := by
460:   rw [dimH_univ_pi, Fintype.card_fin]
461: 
462: theorem dimH_of_mem_nhds {x : E} {s : Set E} (h : s ∈ 𝓝 x) : dimH s = finrank ℝ E := by
463:   have e : E ≃L[ℝ] Fin (finrank ℝ E) → ℝ :=
464:     ContinuousLinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq (Module.finrank_fin_fun ℝ).symm
465:   rw [← e.dimH_image]
466:   refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
467:   · exact (dimH_mono (subset_univ _)).trans_eq (dimH_univ_pi_fin _)
468:   · have : e '' s ∈ 𝓝 (e x) := by rw [← e.map_nhds_eq]; exact image_mem_map h
469:     rcases Metric.nhds_basis_ball.mem_iff.1 this with ⟨r, hr0, hr⟩
470:     simpa only [dimH_ball_pi_fin (e x) hr0] using dimH_mono hr
471: 
472: theorem dimH_of_nonempty_interior {s : Set E} (h : (interior s).Nonempty) : dimH s = finrank ℝ E :=
473:   let ⟨_, hx⟩ := h
474:   dimH_of_mem_nhds (mem_interior_iff_mem_nhds.1 hx)
475: 
476: /-- The Hausdorff dimension of a nonempty convex set equals the dimension of its affine span. -/
477: theorem Convex.dimH_eq_finrank_vectorSpan {s : Set E} (hcvx : Convex ℝ s) (hne : s.Nonempty) :
478:     dimH s = finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ s) := by
479:   have := hne.to_subtype
480:   let φ := AffineIsometryEquiv.constVSub ℝ
481:     (⟨hne.some, subset_affineSpan ℝ s hne.some_mem⟩ : affineSpan ℝ s)
482:   have hs_eq : s = (↑) '' ((↑) ⁻¹' s : Set (affineSpan ℝ s)) :=
483:     (image_preimage_eq_of_subset <| (subset_affineSpan ℝ s).trans Subtype.range_coe.superset).symm
484:   rw [hs_eq, isometry_subtype_coe.dimH_image, ← φ.isometry.dimH_image,
485:       Real.dimH_of_nonempty_interior, direction_affineSpan ℝ s, ← hs_eq]
486:   simp_rw [← AffineIsometryEquiv.coe_toHomeomorph, ← φ.toHomeomorph.image_interior, image_nonempty]
487:   simpa [intrinsicInterior] using (intrinsicInterior_nonempty hcvx).mpr hne
488: 
489: variable (E)
490: 
491: theorem dimH_univ_eq_finrank : dimH (univ : Set E) = finrank ℝ E :=
492:   dimH_of_mem_nhds (@univ_mem _ (𝓝 0))
493: 
494: theorem dimH_univ : dimH (univ : Set ℝ) = 1 := by
495:   rw [dimH_univ_eq_finrank ℝ, Module.finrank_self, Nat.cast_one]
496: 
497: variable {E}
498: 
499: /-- The Hausdorff dimension of any set in a finite-dimensional real normed space is finite. -/
500: theorem dimH_lt_top (s : Set E) : dimH s < ⊤ := by calc
501:   dimH s ≤ dimH (univ : Set E) := dimH_mono (subset_univ s)
502:   _ = finrank ℝ E := dimH_univ_eq_finrank E

1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so

7: [submission](submission-example.md), [source application](source-application-example.md)
8: and [quantified implication](quantified-implication-example.md) examples.
9: These examples show format and derivations, not certified benchmark answers.
10: 
11: The complete [guarded-definition example](guarded-definition-example.md) shows
12: how to organize a target that includes an object's existence and a property
13: of that object. For a real a let Q(r) mean r=a. R001 first proves N001, unique
14: existence of a Q witness, without using w. D002 then defines w as that unique
15: witness with requires=[N001]. R002 takes N001 as a direct input and proves the
16: full target: unique existence and w=a. Listing D002 in the global spec does
17: not let R001 use it before its guard. Do not hide an unproved guard in a
18: restricted domain when the frozen target requires a statement on the full
19: original domain. This pattern adds no new assumption or mathematical source.
20: 
21: ## Construct one coherent candidate
22: 
23: 1. For `target` and `definitions`, extract the original H, ambient parameters
24:    and global typed definitions. Preserve the original source locations. Do
25:    not change a parameter's mathematical kind while fixing its metadata.
26: 2. For `statement_closure`, design N/R interfaces from what their
27:    consumers actually need. Put the complete formulas, quantified conditions
28:    and space identifications into the exported statement, not only its body.
29: 3. For `dependency_closure` and `argument`, construct
30:    each proof unit alongside its premises. List exact source inputs or display
31:    a prior local derivation for every substantive fact beyond the fixed
32:    calculations. Split when local context changes; avoid a giant S whose
33:    changing objects must later be repaired one at a time.
34: 4. For `sources` and `applicability`, inspect each selected native/primary
35:    source, preserve its complete contract and ground each instantiated premise.
36:    A signature lookup or a sentence claiming a hypothesis is true is not proof
37:    of that hypothesis. Reuse an adequate proved source rather than re-proving
38:    it; a project-specific bridge still requires its displayed derivation.
39: 5. For object declarations and local scopes under dependency_closure, introduce objects and conditional premises
40:    at their actual first use. Keep witness bases and local F dependencies
41:    correct. Preserve exact coefficients and ranges when copying calculations.
42: 6. Run check_draft, correct its actual located records, inspect every own
43:    conditional packet, and report readiness below. The independent auditor
44:    applies the same criteria after definitive submission.
45: 
46: ## Canonical data shapes
47: 
48: Submit {spec,graph} using the schema, or preserve an own draft with
49: {base_candidate:N,patches:[...]}. The controller binds identity, input/pin
50: hashes, fixed language and exact native metadata; it does not rewrite proof
51: content. Use read_draft with a narrow pointer after an edit rejection.
52: Unique existing @ID/@symbol selectors work for own-stage reads/patches;
53: inserting array elements still uses numeric indices or /-. Audit evidence
54: uses standard JSON pointers instead of this selector extension.
55: 
56: For multiline changes prefer read_draft(candidate=N,pointer="/graph/inferences/@R001/argument/@S001/text",
57: start_line=1,end_line=20). It returns the actual numbered lines, total_lines
58: and complete text_sha256. Use an edit with exactly
59: {op:"replace_lines",path:"/graph/inferences/@R001/argument/@S001/text",start_line:4,end_line:5,
60: text:"replacement including its intended line endings",text_sha256:"the returned hash"}.
61: Ranges are positive and inclusive. Unselected text and line endings are
62: preserved; stale hashes are rejected. Include a line terminator when a
63: nonempty replacement precedes retained lines. Empty text deletes the range.
64: All ordinary validation and later Audit A still apply.
65: For reads only, an end beyond the string returns its remaining existing lines
66: and the actual range; the start must exist and at most 250 lines may be
67: requested. Line edits still reject any out-of-range end and never clamp it.
68: 
69: Each D has type, full definition, binders, used objects, D dependencies and
70: proved guards. Each H/E/M/N/P has full statement, definitions, binders, objects
71: and appropriate source/origin fields. Each R has direct inputs, one output,
72: definitions, rules, locals, argument and real source applications. Each S has
73: actual text, uses, earlier uses_local, objects, complete produces F statements,
74: and assumption introductions/discharges. Each source application has input,
75: at:Sddd, bindings and actual hypothesis_checks. See the linked schema/examples
76: for exact names. source_uses can serialize one already selected M/E into the
77: R.inputs, S.uses and application together; supply the actual mathematical
78: bindings and grounds yourself.

spec.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
spec.conclusion: dimH(Feuc)=dimH(E)+1, with Feuc in Euclidean Wn and E in Euclidean Vn.

hypotheses.statement: E is compact in Euclidean ℝ^n.

definitions.type: extended diameter, for subsets of a pseudo extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a pseudo extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y): x∈B, y∈B} in [0,∞], with sup ∅=0.

definitions.type: real diameter notation for subsets of a metric space
definitions.definition: For a metric space Z and B⊆Z, diam(B)=(ediam(B)).toReal, where toReal agrees with finite nonnegative reals and sends ∞ to 0. Only finite-extended-diameter sets are assigned real diameters in our covering arguments. Empty sets and singletons have diameter zero.

definitions.type: extended nonnegative content C_p(r,B), also denoted YuiContent p r B
definitions.definition: For a metric (or extended metric) space Z, real p, r∈[0,∞], B⊆Z, define C_p(r,B)=inf_{U:ℕ→Set Z} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} ∑_{i≥0} sup_{h:U_i≠∅}(ediam(U_i))^p. Empty infima are ∞ and empty suprema are 0. Thus empty cover members cost zero, also at p=0. This is exactly YuiContent in basis-registry.json/lean_header. For a real scale δ≥0, C_p(δ,B) means C_p(ofReal δ,B); nonnegative real finite costs are embedded in [0,∞].

definitions.type: unnormalized diameter-power Hausdorff measure μH[p] on Borel extended metric spaces
definitions.definition: μH[p] is the native unnormalized Hausdorff measure, MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure p = Measure.mkMetric (r↦r^p). Its underlying outer measure is obtained from the metric outer measure construction: at each positive scale infimize the sums of diameter powers of countable covers, empty members costing zero, then take the supremum as the scale tends to zero. Evaluation μH[p](B) is the outer-measure value on any B⊆Z, with no measurability assumption on B. The exact native formula, including all extended scales, is registered in M001.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.definition: For an extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, dimH(B)=sup{a∈[0,∞): μH[a](B)=∞}, evaluated in [0,∞] using the Borel measurable structure. The supremum of an empty set of exponents is 0. This is the native Hausdorff dimension and gives the critical-exponent convention of the original problem; N001 identifies its measure with the original covering definition at positive exponents.

For metric spaces Z,Y, maxProd(Z,Y) is Z×Y with distance between (x,t),(y,u) equal to max(dist_Z(x,y),dist_Y(t,u)). For real normed spaces this is the standard max norm on the product. Products in auxiliary propositions use this metric unless explicitly Euclidean.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on ℝ, with its Borel measurable structure
definitions.definition: volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, whose values on arbitrary subsets mean its outer-measure values. For a measurable space Z, measure ν and B⊆Z, ν|B denotes the restricted measure; on measurable S it has value ν(S∩B).
For B⊆Z, indicator(B)(t)=1 when t∈B and 0 otherwise; w indicator(B) is the function equal to w on B and 0 off B, for w∈[0,∞], including w=∞.

For a measure ν on a measurable space Z and f:Z→[0,∞], lintegral_ν(f)=∫⁻ f dν is the supremum of integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions bounded pointwise by f. The integral of a simple function is the finite sum of its distinct nonzero values times the measure of the corresponding fibers. ∫⁻_B f dν means lintegral_{ν|B}(f).
For a finite dimensional real vector space Z, finrank(Z)=Module.finrank ℝ Z is the natural-number cardinality of any finite basis. Natural values are embedded into [0,∞] in dimension inequalities.
For a metric space Z, center u∈Z and radius a∈ℝ, closedBall(u,a)={x∈Z: dist(x,u)≤a}.
Vn=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), identified with ℝ^n with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. Fin n={0,...,n−1}; for n=0 it is empty and Vn consists of the zero tuple.
Wn=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin(n+1)), with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure.

T(x,t) has coordinates T(x,t)(i.castSucc)=x(i) for i∈Fin n and T(x,t)(Fin.last n)=t, where i.castSucc retains the index i<n in Fin(n+1) and Fin.last n is its last index n. This defines a total map without presupposing linearity or invertibility.
Fmax=E×I in maxProd(Vn,ℝ).
Feuc={z∈Wn : (i↦z(i.castSucc))∈E and z(Fin.last n)∈I}. This is exactly the Euclidean product subset E×[0,1] in the original target.

propositions.statement: For every extended metric space Z with measurable structure equal to its Borel structure, every p∈ℝ and B⊆Z, μH[p](B)=sup_{r∈[0,∞], r>0} C_p(r,B). The content is exactly the nested infimum over ℕ-indexed covers of extended diameter ≤r and the sum of the nonempty-member supremum of (ediam U_i)^p.

propositions.statement: For every metric space X with its Borel structure, A⊆X and real p>0, at each finite positive real scale δ, C_p(δ,A) is exactly the infimum of ∑_i diam(U_i)^p over countable δ-covers of A, with empty members costing zero. Each cover bounds content above. It is antitone in δ; μH[p](A)=sup_{δ∈ℝ,δ>0} C_p(δ,A). Moreover μH[p](A)=0 iff for every δ>0 and ε>0 an admissible ℕ-indexed cover has cost <ε. Suprema along scales decreasing to zero give the same measure. These agree exactly with the original H^p_δ and H^p, without a normalization factor. Countable subfamilies and pairs (i,j) with j<N_i may be enumerated by ℕ and padded by empty sets without changing coverage or nonnegative cost.

locals.type: metric space with its Borel measurable structure
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X and equip it with its Borel structure.
Fix any A⊆X.
Fix a real exponent p, and temporarily assume L1: p>0.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary metric space X with its Borel structure, a subset A and a real p. Temporarily assume L1: p>0. M001 applies to this metric space viewed as an extended metric space; its inner nested infima and empty-member supremum are exactly D004. Hence μH[p](A)=sup_{r∈[0,∞],r>0} C_p(r,A).

Any admissible cover bounds the defining infimum from above. For positive scales δ₁≤δ₂, every δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover, so C_p(δ₂,A)≤C_p(δ₁,A), also when a family of covers is empty. Finite positive real scales are cofinal towards zero among positive extended scales: below a finite r>0 take its real value or half that value, and below r=∞ take 1. Thus every content appearing in F001 is bounded by one at a finite positive scale, while every finite positive scale already occurs there. It follows that μH[p](A)=sup_{δ∈ℝ,δ>0} C_p(δ,A). The same antitonicity shows that for every real sequence δ_k>0 tending to zero, the supremum of its contents equals this supremum: below any fixed δ>0 one eventually has δ_k≤δ.

produces.statement: For every δ>0, an admissible δ-cover bounds C_p(δ,A) above; for 0<δ₁≤δ₂, C_p(δ₂,A)≤C_p(δ₁,A). Also μH[p](A)=sup_{δ∈ℝ,δ>0} C_p(δ,A), and any positive real sequence tending to zero has the same supremum of contents.

argument.text: For the forward small-cover assertion temporarily suppose L2: μH[p](A)=0. By F002, every finite-scale content is zero. At a fixed positive δ and ε, if no admissible cost were <ε then every admissible cost would be ≥ε and its infimum would be ≥ε; if there were no admissible family the infimum would be ∞. Both contradict zero content. Thus there is a cover of cost <ε for every δ>0, ε>0. Discharge L2 into this implication. Conversely temporarily suppose L3: such covers exist for all δ>0 and ε>0. Each content is then ≤ε for every ε>0, and is nonnegative, so is zero by order density in [0,∞]. F002 gives μH[p](A)=0. Discharge L3. This establishes both directions without assuming a minimizer of an infimum.

produces.statement: μH[p](A)=0 iff for every finite δ>0 and ε>0 an admissible ℕ-indexed δ-cover of A has total p-cost <ε.

argument.text: At finite scale every nonempty cover member has finite ediam, equal to the embedding of its real diam. Since p>0, zero diameter has p-power zero; the supremum over a nonempty-member proposition is exactly that diameter power, and for an empty member it is zero. Thus the infimum in D004 is precisely the original ordinary-diameter infimum H^p_δ, and F002 identifies μH[p] with the original H^p with no factor. Any countable subfamily, or the pairs (i,j) with i∈ℕ and 0≤j<N_i for a natural-number family N, has a countable index set: it is a subset of ℕ or ℕ×ℕ. Inject it into ℕ, place each set at its assigned index, and use ∅ elsewhere. The union is unchanged and each nonzero cost occurs once; the sum, defined as the supremum of finite subsums, is unchanged. These conclusions, F002 and F003 hold for all the arbitrary objects. Discharge L1 into p>0 and universally quantify to obtain every clause of N001.

applications.bindings: Set Z=X, B=A and the real exponent to p; identify C with the exact nested infimum in D004.
hypothesis_checks: X is a metric space, hence an extended metric space, and its selected measurable structure is its Borel structure.

locals.type: metric space with its Borel structure
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X.
Fix A⊆X.
Fix real q and temporarily assume L1: q>0 and μH[q](A)=0.
Fix real r and temporarily assume as part of L2 that 0<r≤1.
Fix real ε and temporarily assume as part of L2 that ε>0.
Choose an r/2-cover U of A with q-cost <ε/2 supplied by F001.
Put d_i=diam(U_i); empty members have d_i=0.
Choose the positive radii a_i satisfying F002 for all natural i.

locals.type: family of points of X indexed by {i∈ℕ:U_i≠∅}
locals.declaration: Choose u_i∈U_i for every nonempty U_i as in F003.
Set K_i=closedBall(u_i,a_i) when U_i≠∅ and K_i=∅ otherwise.
Set N_i=ceil(1/a_i).

locals.type: family of subsets of maxProd(X,ℝ) indexed by pairs (i,j), i∈ℕ, 0≤j<N_i
locals.declaration: Set blocks_{i,j}=K_i×[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i].
For the final small-cover test fix any target scale Δ>0.
Fix any cost tolerance τ>0.
Set rTarget=min(1,Δ/2).
Set εTarget=τ/(2·2^(q+2)).

argument.text: Fix X,A,q and temporarily assume L1: q>0 and μH[q](A)=0. Fix arbitrary r,ε under L2: 0<r≤1 and ε>0. By N001 at scale r/2 and tolerance ε/2 there exists an ℕ-indexed r/2-cover of A of q-cost <ε/2.

produces.statement: There exists an ℕ-indexed cover U of A with ediam(U_i)≤r/2 for every i and ∑_i diam(U_i)^q<ε/2, empty members costing zero.

argument.text: Choose U as in F001 and put d_i=diam(U_i). All diameters are finite and 0≤d_i≤r/2; empty members have diameter zero. For each i, continuity from the right of x↦x^q on [0,∞) (q>0) and d_i<r allow a_i∈(d_i,r) with a_i^q<d_i^q+ε·2^(−i−2). At d_i=0 the same assertion follows from x^q→0 as x↓0. Countable choice gives a single family of such radii; in particular each satisfies d_i<a_i≤r.

produces.statement: There exists a real family a with for every i∈ℕ, 0≤d_i<a_i≤r and a_i^q<d_i^q+ε·2^(−i−2).

argument.text: Choose a as in F002. Taking finite subsums and then their supremum yields ∑_i a_i^q≤∑_i d_i^q+ε∑_i2^(−i−2)=∑_i d_i^q+ε/2<ε. The geometric sum is 1/2; it follows by summing the finite geometric series and taking its increasing limit. The strict final inequality comes from F001, not from summing strictly termwise inequalities. For each nonempty U_i there exists a point in U_i by the meaning of nonempty, so countable choice provides a family of centers on precisely those indices.

produces.statement: ∑_i a_i^q<ε, and there exists a family u_i∈U_i for all i with U_i≠∅.

binders.type: family on nonempty indices of U with values in X

argument.text: Choose the family u from F003. For nonempty U_i put K_i=closedBall(u_i,a_i); put K_i=∅ for empty U_i. Distances within U_i are ≤d_i<a_i, hence U_i⊆K_i. The triangle inequality gives diam(K_i)≤2a_i; this does not require a ball of positive actual diameter and works for a singleton X. Define N_i=ceil(1/a_i), positive because a_i>0. The N_i closed intervals [j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i], 0≤j<N_i, cover I and have diameter 1/N_i≤a_i. Since a_i≤r≤1, N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i. Define blocks_{i,j}=K_i times those intervals. They cover A×I and in maxProd(X,ℝ) each has diameter ≤2a_i≤2r, by the maximum formula for distances. There are countably many blocks, and N001 permits reindexing them by ℕ with empty padding.

produces.statement: blocks is a countable cover of A×I with diam(blocks_{i,j})≤2a_i≤2r, and 1≤N_i≤2/a_i for every i.

argument.text:
By F004, q+1>0 and the nonnegative real-power laws,
∑_i∑_{j<N_i} diam(blocks_{i,j})^(q+1)
 ≤∑_i N_i(2a_i)^(q+1)
 ≤2^(q+2)∑_i a_i^q
 <2^(q+2)ε.
The second inequality follows termwise from N_i≤2/a_i and a_i>0, since (2/a_i)(2a_i)^(q+1)=2^(q+2)a_i^q. Empty original indices have K_i=∅ and cost zero. All inequalities of infinite nonnegative sums follow from finite subsums, so remain valid without a preliminary summability assumption. This gives the quantitative cover for the arbitrary r,ε. Discharge L2 and universally quantify them; the resulting quantitative statement is F005.

produces.statement: For every 0<r≤1 and ε>0, A×I in maxProd(X,ℝ) has a countable 2r-cover of (q+1)-cost <2^(q+2)ε. The constant depends only on q.

argument.text: For any positive target scale Δ and tolerance τ, set rTarget=min(1,Δ/2)>0 and εTarget=τ/(2·2^(q+2))>0. F005 gives a cover of diameter ≤2rTarget≤Δ and cost <2^(q+2)εTarget=τ/2<τ. N001, now in maxProd(X,ℝ) with its Borel structure and positive exponent q+1, yields μH[q+1](A×I)=0. This and F005 are the two clauses of N002. Discharge L1 and quantify X,A,q; Δ,τ were arbitrary small-cover test values, not new hypotheses.

locals.type: metric space with its Borel structure
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X with its Borel structure.
Fix any subset A⊆X.
Fix a real exponent s.
Fix a real finite scale δ and temporarily assume L1: s>0 and δ>0.
Fix any family U; temporarily assume L2: U covers A×I and each ediam(U_i)≤δ.
Set cost=∑_i diam(U_i)^(s+1), with empty summands zero.
Set c=C_s(δ,A), without a finiteness assumption.
Set px(x,t)=x.
Set pt(x,t)=t.
Set ρ_i=diam(U_i), equal to zero when U_i is empty.
Set Ax_i=px '' U_i.
Set Bt_i=pt '' U_i.
Fix arbitrary ε under L3: ε>0.
For nonempty U_i set J_i=(inf Bt_i−η_i/2,sup Bt_i+η_i/2); for empty U_i set J_i=∅.
Set Ws_i(t)=Ax_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise.
Set g_i(t)=ρ_i^s indicator(J_i∩I)(t).

argument.text: Fix X,A,s,δ and temporarily assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Put the product A×I in maxProd(X,ℝ). Fix an arbitrary ℕ-indexed family U under L2: it covers A×I and ediam(U_i)≤δ for every i. Let cost=∑_i diam(U_i)^(s+1), with empty terms zero, and c=C_s(δ,A). The cover diameters are finite, but c and cost may be infinite. Define px(x,t)=x and pt(x,t)=t. The distance in either coordinate is at most the maximum of the two coordinate distances, so both projections are 1-Lipschitz in extended distance.

produces.statement: Both coordinate projections px and pt are 1-Lipschitz for the max product.

argument.text: Define ρ_i=diam(U_i), Ax_i=px '' U_i and Bt_i=pt '' U_i. Applying M016 to each projection, justified by F001, gives ediam(Ax_i)≤ediam(U_i) and ediam(Bt_i)≤ediam(U_i); thus diam(Ax_i),diam(Bt_i)≤ρ_i≤δ. Empty U_i gives empty projections and ρ_i=0. For any nonempty index the set Bt_i is nonempty and bounded: a point b₀∈Bt_i exists, and |b−b₀|≤ρ_i for every b∈Bt_i. Its real infimum and supremum therefore bound all its points. Taking suprema in b−b'≤ρ_i gives sup Bt_i−inf Bt_i≤ρ_i. This uses only completeness of ℝ for nonempty bounded sets, not measurability of a projection.

produces.statement: For every i, 0≤ρ_i≤δ and ediam(Ax_i),ediam(Bt_i)≤ofReal ρ_i. For nonempty U_i, Bt_i is nonempty and bounded with all its points between inf Bt_i and sup Bt_i and sup Bt_i−inf Bt_i≤ρ_i; for empty U_i both projections are empty and ρ_i=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary ε under L3: ε>0, and define η_i=ε·2^(−i−1)/(1+ρ_i^s)>0. For a nonempty U_i define J_i=(inf Bt_i−η_i/2,sup Bt_i+η_i/2); for an empty U_i define J_i=∅. F002 shows Bt_i⊆J_i, including when Bt_i is a singleton, and the interval's length is at most ρ_i+η_i. These intervals and ∅ are Borel sets. No U_i or projection is required to be measurable.

produces.statement: For every i, J_i is Borel, Bt_i⊆J_i and, if U_i is nonempty, the open interval J_i has length at most ρ_i+η_i; if U_i is empty, J_i=∅. Each η_i is positive.

argument.text: For each t∈I define Ws_i(t)=Ax_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise. For every x∈A the covering property supplies an index i with (x,t)∈U_i, whence x∈Ax_i and t∈Bt_i⊆J_i. Thus this is a δ-cover of A. Its s-cost is ≤∑_iρ_i^s indicator(J_i)(t), using F002 and s>0 also at zero diameters. N001 therefore gives c≤∑_iρ_i^s indicator(J_i)(t) for t∈I. Define the zero-extended summands g_i(t)=ρ_i^s indicator(J_i∩I)(t). Then c indicator(I)(t)≤∑_i g_i(t) for all real t: the preceding inequality holds on I and both sides vanish off I. Each g_i is measurable, since J_i∩I is Borel and its finite weight ρ_i^s is constant.

produces.statement: For every t∈ℝ, c indicator(I)(t)≤∑_i g_i(t), where g_i(t)=ρ_i^s indicator(J_i∩I)(t); each g_i is Borel measurable and c=C_s(δ,A).

argument.text:
We may compute the integral over I or equivalently the integral of the zero extension over ℝ. M014 with endpoints 0,1 gives volume(I)=1. M013 with ν=volume, set I and constant c gives ∫⁻_I c dvolume=c·1=c even for c=∞. M011 for the measurable set I computes the integral of c indicator(I) to the same value. Apply M012 to the pointwise inequality F004, M010 to the ℕ-indexed measurable functions g_i, and M011 to each Borel set J_i∩I with constant ρ_i^s. We obtain
 c≤∫⁻ (∑_i g_i) dvolume
   =∑_i ∫⁻ g_i dvolume
   =∑_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I).
Every use is a nonnegative integral, so no finite-integral or absolute-summability condition is imposed.

produces.statement: c≤∑_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I), with c possibly ∞.

argument.text:
By measure monotonicity volume(J_i∩I)≤volume(J_i). For each nonempty index M015 gives volume(J_i)=ofReal(sup Bt_i−inf Bt_i+η_i)≤ofReal(ρ_i+η_i), using F003; at empty indices volume(J_i)=0. Thus
 c≤∑_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I)
  ≤∑_i ρ_i^s(ρ_i+η_i)
  =∑_iρ_i^(s+1)+∑_iη_iρ_i^s
  ≤cost+ε.
Here the power identity also holds at ρ_i=0 since s>0. The error is termwise bounded by ε·2^(−i−1), since η_iρ_i^s=ε·2^(−i−1)ρ_i^s/(1+ρ_i^s)≤ε·2^(−i−1). Its sum is ≤ε, because ∑_{i≥0}2^(−i−1)=1, as follows from finite geometric sums and their increasing limit. Splitting and comparing nonnegative sums is justified by taking suprema of finite subsums, including infinite totals. The first main sum is cost by its definition. Discharge L3 and quantify the arbitrary ε to get F006.

produces.statement: For every ε>0, c≤cost+ε in [0,∞].

argument.text: F006 implies c≤cost. If cost=∞ this is immediate. If cost<∞ but c>cost, order density permits a finite positive ε with cost+ε<c (also when c=∞), contradicting F006. This argument needs no finiteness of c. Since U was arbitrary, discharge L2 and quantify U: every admissible δ-cover of A×I has (s+1)-cost at least C_s(δ,A).

produces.statement: Every ℕ-indexed δ-cover U of A×I in maxProd(X,ℝ) satisfies C_s(δ,A)≤∑_i diam(U_i)^(s+1), with empty terms zero.

argument.text: Infimizing the bound F007 over the admissible families gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I), using the ordinary-cost identification N001. If there is no admissible family the right side is ∞ and the same inequality holds. Thus the bound holds for every finite δ>0; take suprema over these scales and apply N001 at the positive exponents s and s+1 to obtain μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I). Discharge L1 and quantify the arbitrary X,A,s,δ. This proves both clauses of N003, without adding any measurability or compactness premise.

applications.bindings: Z=maxProd(X,ℝ), Y=X, K=1, f=px, B=U_i for each natural i.
hypothesis_checks: The given metric spaces induce pseudo extended metric structures.
K=1 is nonnegative.
F001 proves the projection inequality directly from the maximum formula.

hypothesis_checks: The max product and ℝ have their metric-induced pseudo extended metric structures.
K=1 is nonnegative.
F001 proves the second coordinate projection inequality.

Z=ℝ, ν=volume, B=I, constant c=C_s(δ,A), possibly infinite.
hypothesis_checks: ℝ has its Borel structure and volume is Lebesgue measure by D008.

applications.bindings: Z=ℝ, ν=volume, B=I, constant c, computing the zero extension of the restricted constant.
hypothesis_checks: D008 supplies the Borel Lebesgue measure.
I is closed, hence Borel measurable.

hypothesis_checks: The Borel Lebesgue measure is D008.
F004 proves the inequality on all ℝ, including off I by zero extension.

hypothesis_checks: D008 supplies the measurable space and measure.
The index type is ℕ, which is countable.
F004 proves Borel measurability of every g_i, hence volume-a.e. measurability.

hypothesis_checks: D008 supplies Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line.
F003 gives J_i Borel, and I is closed; their intersection is Borel.

locals.declaration: Fix any finite dimensional real normed space V.
Fix any A⊆V.

argument.text: Fix V and A⊆V. The inclusion A⊆univ V and M006 give dimH(A)≤dimH(univ V). M008 identifies the latter with finrank(V). This is a natural number and hence <∞ when embedded in [0,∞]; nonnegativity follows from the codomain of dimH. Thus 0≤dimH(A)≤finrank(V)<∞, including finrank(V)=0, where the inequalities force dimH(A)=0. Quantify V,A to obtain N004.

applications.bindings: Z=V, B=A, Q=univ V.
hypothesis_checks: The norm on V supplies its metric and hence extended metric.
Every point of A is a point of V, so A⊆univ V.

applications.bindings: Take the source space to be V.
hypothesis_checks: V is the arbitrary finite dimensional real normed space declared in this inference.

argument.text: The open interval (0,1) is contained in I, so 1/2 belongs to the interior of I: for instance its radius-1/4 open ball lies inside I. Apply M009 to the real normed space ℝ and the set I. The singleton basis {1} spans ℝ over ℝ and is independent, so finrank(ℝ)=1. The result is dimH(I)=1.

applications.bindings: V=ℝ and B=I=[0,1].
hypothesis_checks: ℝ is a real normed space with finite basis {1}, so is finite dimensional.
The radius-1/4 ball about 1/2 is inside I; hence 1/2 is an interior point.

locals.type: finite dimensional real normed space with its Borel structure
locals.declaration: Fix any finite dimensional real normed space V.
Fix A⊆V and temporarily assume L1: A is nonempty and compact.
Set d=(dimH(A)).toReal.
Set h=dimH(A×I) in maxProd(V,ℝ).
Fix arbitrary real q under L2: q>d.
Set hreal=h.toReal; finiteness of h is first proved in S004.
Under the contradiction branch L3 set qUpper=(d+hreal−1)/2.
Under L4: d>0, fix arbitrary real s under L5: 0<s<d.
Under L6: hreal<d+1, set sLower=(max(0,hreal−1)+d)/2.
Under the zero-dimension branch choose x0∈A, whose existence was recorded in F001.
Set j(t)=(x0,t).

argument.text: Fix V,A and assume L1: A is nonempty compact. Put d=(dimH(A)).toReal and h=dimH(A×I) in the max product. N004 gives dimH(A)≤finrank(V)<∞; hence d≥0 and dimH(A) is exactly the finite nonnegative-real embedding of d. Nonemptiness in L1 also gives existence of a point of A. We retain compactness in the conditional theorem, although the following dimension argument only needs the finite ambient bound and nonemptiness.

produces.statement: d≥0, dimH(A)=ofReal d<∞, and there exists x0∈A.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary real q under L2: q>d. By F001, q>0 and dimH(A)<q. Equip V with its Borel structure and regard q as a nonnegative real, without changing its real exponent. M003 gives μH[q](A)=0.

produces.statement: q>0 and μH[q](A)=0.

argument.text: N002 at X=V, exponent q and set A gives μH[q+1](A×I)=0. Since 0≠∞, M004 applied in maxProd(V,ℝ), at nonnegative exponent q+1, gives h≤q+1. Discharge L2 and quantify q: this bound holds for every q>d.

produces.statement: For every real q>d, h≤ofReal(q+1).

argument.text: F003 with q=d+1 gives h≤d+2<∞. Set hreal=h.toReal, so h=ofReal hreal and hreal≥0. Temporarily assume L3: hreal>d+1. The real number qUpper=(d+hreal−1)/2 lies strictly between d and hreal−1. F003 would give hreal≤qUpper+1<hreal, a contradiction. Discharge L3, obtaining hreal≤d+1 and thus h≤ofReal(d+1). This is the limiting upper bound, using no subtraction of infinite extended numbers.

produces.statement: h<∞, h=ofReal hreal, hreal≥0 and hreal≤d+1.

argument.text: First take the branch L4: d>0. Fix arbitrary real s under L5: 0<s<d. In V with its Borel structure, F001 gives s<dimH(A); regard s as a nonnegative real. M002 gives μH[s](A)=∞.

produces.statement: s>0 and μH[s](A)=∞.

argument.text: N003 at X=V, set A and exponent s gives μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I); hence the latter measure is ∞ by F005. M005 at exponent s+1 in maxProd(V,ℝ) gives s+1≤h. Discharge L5 and universally quantify s to record the full family of lower bounds.

produces.statement: For every real s with 0<s<d, ofReal(s+1)≤h.

argument.text: Under L4, suppose temporarily L6: hreal<d+1. Since d>0, max(0,hreal−1)<d. Put sLower=(max(0,hreal−1)+d)/2. Then 0<sLower<d and sLower+1>hreal, contradicting F006 and the finite identification in F004. Discharge L6 to obtain d+1≤hreal. Discharge L4 into the implication: if d>0 then ofReal(d+1)≤h. This is the lower limiting step.

produces.statement: If d>0 then ofReal(d+1)≤h.

argument.text: For the other branch assume L7: d=0. By the existence assertion in F001 choose x0∈A. Define j:ℝ→maxProd(V,ℝ) by j(t)=(x0,t). For all real t,u the product distance is max(dist_V(x0,x0),|t−u|)=|t−u|, so j is an isometry. Since x0∈A, j '' I⊆A×I.

produces.statement: j is an isometry from ℝ to maxProd(V,ℝ), and j '' I⊆A×I.

argument.text: M007 applied to j gives dimH(j '' I)=dimH(I). N005 is dimH(I)=1. M006 applied to the inclusion F008 gives dimH(j '' I)≤dimH(A×I)=h. Thus 1≤h; since d=0, ofReal(d+1)≤h. Discharge L7 into that implication. The identity of the private x0 is immaterial to the exported inequality.

produces.statement: If d=0 then ofReal(d+1)≤h.

argument.text: By F001, d≥0, so either d>0 or d=0. F007 and F009 give ofReal(d+1)≤h in the respective exhaustive branches. F004 gives the reverse inequality, and F001 identifies dimH(A) with d. Thus dimH(A×I)=dimH(A)+1. If finrank(V)=0 then N004 gives d=0 and the same zero branch applies; no positive-dimensional ball was needed in N002 or N003. Discharge L1 and quantify V,A to prove N006 with precisely its stated nonempty compact premise.

applications.bindings: Z=V, B=A, a=q as a nonnegative real.
hypothesis_checks: The normed space V is a metric space with its chosen Borel structure.
F001 and L2 give q>d≥0.
F001 identifies dimH(A)=d and L2 is q>d.

applications.bindings: Z=maxProd(V,ℝ), B=A×I, a=q+1 as a nonnegative real.
hypothesis_checks: The max product is metric and is equipped with its Borel structure.
F002 gives q>0, so q+1>0.
N002 applied to F002 gives μH[q+1](A×I)=0, and 0≠∞.

applications.bindings: Z=V, B=A, a=s as a nonnegative real.
hypothesis_checks: V is metric with its Borel structure.
L5 gives s>0.
F001 gives dimH(A)=d and L5 gives s<d.

applications.bindings: Z=maxProd(V,ℝ), B=A×I, a=s+1 as a nonnegative real.
hypothesis_checks: The max product is metric with its Borel structure.
F005 gives s>0, so s+1>0.
N003 gives μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I), and F005 makes the left side ∞.

applications.bindings: Z=ℝ, Y=maxProd(V,ℝ), f=j, B=I.
hypothesis_checks: Both ℝ and the max product are metric, hence extended metric spaces.
F008 proves j preserves every distance by max(0,|t−u|)=|t−u|.

hypothesis_checks: The max product carries its metric-induced extended metric.
F008 proves this inclusion from x0∈A.

locals.declaration: Define Tinverse(z)=((i↦z(i.castSucc)),z(Fin.last n)), interpreting the first tuple in Euclidean Vn.
For the metric comparison fix arbitrary x∈Vn.
Fix arbitrary y∈Vn.
Fix arbitrary real t.
Fix arbitrary real u.
Set a=||x−y||₂.
Set b=|t−u|.

argument.text: Use Vn,Wn and the total coordinate map T from D013–D015. Define Tinverse(z)=((i↦z(i.castSucc)),z(Fin.last n)). Every index of Fin(n+1) is either its last index n or uniquely i.castSucc with i∈Fin n. In these cases substitution proves T(Tinverse(z))=z; substitution on the first n coordinates and the last coordinate proves Tinverse(T(x,t))=(x,t). Addition and real scalar multiplication are coordinatewise, so T is linear and these inverse identities make it a real linear equivalence. For n=0 the first family of coordinate equations is empty and the last one proves the same identities.

produces.statement: T:maxProd(Vn,ℝ)→Wn is a real linear equivalence, with inverse Tinverse(z)=((i↦z(i.castSucc)),z(Fin.last n)), including n=0.

argument.text: Vn has its n standard coordinate vectors as a real basis and Wn has its n+1 standard coordinate vectors; the empty coordinate basis is a basis when n=0. A basis of Vn×ℝ consists of each coordinate basis vector in the first factor with last coordinate zero, together with the vector (0,1). Coordinate expansion gives spanning and comparison of each coordinate gives independence. Thus both maxProd(Vn,ℝ) and Wn are finite dimensional real normed spaces, using the standard max norm on the former. By the definitions of Fmax and Feuc, T '' Fmax=Feuc: T maps a pair in E×I to exactly those first n coordinates and last coordinate, and for any z∈Feuc its explicit inverse belongs to E×I. This identifies the actual subset, rather than merely some linear-equivalent set.

produces.statement: maxProd(Vn,ℝ) and Wn are finite dimensional real normed spaces, and T '' Fmax=Feuc.

argument.text: Apply the prepared finite-dimensional real linear-equivalence adapter E001 to the source space maxProd(Vn,ℝ), target Wn, equivalence T from F001 and subset Fmax. F002 supplies exactly its finite-dimensional normed-space conditions. It gives dimH(T '' Fmax)=dimH(Fmax), hence dimH(Feuc)=dimH(Fmax) by F002. The selected E001 is precisely B008 from the frozen registry; no class-3 claim is being imported.

produces.statement: dimH(Feuc)=dimH(Fmax).

argument.text:
For the explicit metric comparison fix arbitrary x,y∈Vn and real t,u, and write a=||x−y||₂≥0 and b=|t−u|≥0. The domain distance is max(a,b). The sum of squared coordinate differences in Wn splits into its first n coordinates and the last coordinate, so the target distance between T(x,t),T(y,u) is sqrt(a²+b²). Each of a² and b² is at most a²+b², while a²+b²≤2 max(a,b)²; taking nonnegative square roots yields
 max(a,b)≤sqrt(a²+b²)≤sqrt(2) max(a,b).
Thus the coordinate map and its inverse have Lipschitz constants sqrt(2) and 1 respectively. These finite constants are independent of E,n and the points. The formulas hold also at n=0, where a=0. This verifies the metric representation explicitly; F001–F003 supply the equivalence, exact image identification and dimension equality. Together they prove every clause of N007, with the source Vn Euclidean throughout.

applications.bindings: In E001 set V=maxProd(Vn,ℝ), W=Wn, e=T (the linear equivalence proved in F001), and take the subset A=Fmax=E×I.
hypothesis_checks: F002 constructs finite coordinate bases for both real normed spaces, with the max norm on the source and Euclidean norm on the target; n=0 is included.
F001 proves coordinate linearity and both inverse identities for exactly T, with the displayed Tinverse.

argument.text: Apply N006 to V=Vn and A=E. Vn is the Euclidean real normed space with its finite coordinate basis, and the original hypotheses H001,H002 give respectively nonemptiness and compactness. Therefore dimH(Fmax)=dimH(E)+1. N007 gives dimH(Feuc)=dimH(Fmax), with Feuc precisely the original Euclidean product subset in Wn. Substitution yields dimH(Feuc)=dimH(E)+1, the complete selected equality for every natural n including zero, with the original Euclidean metrics and no additional hypotheses.

e is a real linear equivalence V≃ₗ[ℝ]W.
value.statement: For finite dimensional real normed spaces V,W, every real linear equivalence e:V≃ₗ[ℝ]W preserves Hausdorff dimension of images of all subsets.

value.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dimH(Feuc)=dimH(E)+1, with Feuc in Euclidean Wn and E in Euclidean Vn.

hypotheses.statement: E is compact in Euclidean ℝ^n.

definitions.type: extended diameter, for subsets of a pseudo extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a pseudo extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y): x∈B, y∈B} in [0,∞], with sup ∅=0.

definitions.type: real diameter notation for subsets of a metric space
definitions.definition: For a metric space Z and B⊆Z, diam(B)=(ediam(B)).toReal, where toReal agrees with finite nonnegative reals and sends ∞ to 0. Only finite-extended-diameter sets are assigned real diameters in our covering arguments. Empty sets and singletons have diameter zero.

definitions.type: extended nonnegative content C_p(r,B), also denoted YuiContent p r B
definitions.definition: For a metric (or extended metric) space Z, real p, r∈[0,∞], B⊆Z, define C_p(r,B)=inf_{U:ℕ→Set Z} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} ∑_{i≥0} sup_{h:U_i≠∅}(ediam(U_i))^p. Empty infima are ∞ and empty suprema are 0. Thus empty cover members cost zero, also at p=0. This is exactly YuiContent in basis-registry.json/lean_header. For a real scale δ≥0, C_p(δ,B) means C_p(ofReal δ,B); nonnegative real finite costs are embedded in [0,∞].

definitions.type: unnormalized diameter-power Hausdorff measure μH[p] on Borel extended metric spaces
definitions.definition: μH[p] is the native unnormalized Hausdorff measure, MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure p = Measure.mkMetric (r↦r^p). Its underlying outer measure is obtained from the metric outer measure construction: at each positive scale infimize the sums of diameter powers of countable covers, empty members costing zero, then take the supremum as the scale tends to zero. Evaluation μH[p](B) is the outer-measure value on any B⊆Z, with no measurability assumption on B. The exact native formula, including all extended scales, is registered in M001.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.definition: For an extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, dimH(B)=sup{a∈[0,∞): μH[a](B)=∞}, evaluated in [0,∞] using the Borel measurable structure. The supremum of an empty set of exponents is 0. definitions.definition: volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, whose values on arbitrary subsets mean its outer-measure values. For a measurable space Z, measure ν and B⊆Z, ν|B denotes the restricted measure; on measurable S it has value ν(S∩B).
For B⊆Z, indicator(B)(t)=1 when t∈B and 0 otherwise; w indicator(B) is the function equal to w on B and 0 off B, for w∈[0,∞], including w=∞.

For a measure ν on a measurable space Z and f:Z→[0,∞], lintegral_ν(f)=∫⁻ f dν is the supremum of integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions bounded pointwise by f. The integral of a simple function is the finite sum of its distinct nonzero values times the measure of the corresponding fibers. ∫⁻_B f dν means lintegral_{ν|B}(f).
For a finite dimensional real vector space Z, finrank(Z)=Module.finrank ℝ Z is the natural-number cardinality of any finite basis. Natural values are embedded into [0,∞] in dimension inequalities.
For a metric space Z, center u∈Z and radius a∈ℝ, closedBall(u,a)={x∈Z: dist(x,u)≤a}.
Vn=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), identified with ℝ^n with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. Fin n={0,...,n−1}; for n=0 it is empty and Vn consists of the zero tuple.

T(x,t) has coordinates T(x,t)(i.castSucc)=x(i) for i∈Fin n and T(x,t)(Fin.last n)=t, where i.castSucc retains the index i<n in Fin(n+1) and Fin.last n is its last index n. This defines a total map without presupposing linearity or invertibility.

original_context.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.

Put d_i=diam(U_i); empty members have d_i=0.
Choose the positive radii a_i satisfying F002 for all natural i.

locals.type: family of points of X indexed by {i∈ℕ:U_i≠∅}
locals.declaration: Choose u_i∈U_i for every nonempty U_i as in F003.
Set K_i=closedBall(u_i,a_i) when U_i≠∅ and K_i=∅ otherwise.
Set N_i=ceil(1/a_i).

locals.type: family of subsets of maxProd(X,ℝ) indexed by pairs (i,j), i∈ℕ, 0≤j<N_i
locals.declaration: Set blocks_{i,j}=K_i×[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i].
For the final small-cover test fix any target scale Δ>0.
Fix any cost tolerance τ>0.
Set rTarget=min(1,Δ/2).
Set εTarget=τ/(2·2^(q+2)).

argument.text: Fix X,A,q and temporarily assume L1: q>0 and μH[q](A)=0. Fix arbitrary r,ε under L2: 0<r≤1 and ε>0. By N001 at scale r/2 and tolerance ε/2 there exists an ℕ-indexed r/2-cover of A of q-cost <ε/2.

produces.statement: There exists an ℕ-indexed cover U of A with ediam(U_i)≤r/2 for every i and ∑_i diam(U_i)^q<ε/2, empty members costing zero.

argument.text: Choose U as in F001 and put d_i=diam(U_i). All diameters are finite and 0≤d_i≤r/2; empty members have diameter zero. For each i, continuity from the right of x↦x^q on [0,∞) (q>0) and d_i<r allow a_i∈(d_i,r) with a_i^q<d_i^q+ε·2^(−i−2). At d_i=0 the same assertion follows from x^q→0 as x↓0. Countable choice gives a single family of such radii; in particular each satisfies d_i<a_i≤r.

produces.statement: There exists a real family a with for every i∈ℕ, 0≤d_i<a_i≤r and a_i^q<d_i^q+ε·2^(−i−2).

argument.text: Choose a as in F002. Taking finite subsums and then their supremum yields ∑_i a_i^q≤∑_i d_i^q+ε∑_i2^(−i−2)=∑_i d_i^q+ε/2<ε. The geometric sum is 1/2; it follows by summing the finite geometric series and taking its increasing limit. The strict final inequality comes from F001, not from summing strictly termwise inequalities. For each nonempty U_i there exists a point in U_i by the meaning of nonempty, so countable choice provides a family of centers on precisely those indices.

produces.statement: ∑_i a_i^q<ε, and there exists a family u_i∈U_i for all i with U_i≠∅.

binders.type: family on nonempty indices of U with values in X

argument.text: Choose the family u from F003. For nonempty U_i put K_i=closedBall(u_i,a_i); put K_i=∅ for empty U_i. Distances within U_i are ≤d_i<a_i, hence U_i⊆K_i. The triangle inequality gives diam(K_i)≤2a_i; this does not require a ball of positive actual diameter and works for a singleton X. Define N_i=ceil(1/a_i), positive because a_i>0. The N_i closed intervals [j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i], 0≤j<N_i, cover I and have diameter 1/N_i≤a_i. Since a_i≤r≤1, N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i. Define blocks_{i,j}=K_i times those intervals. They cover A×I and in maxProd(X,ℝ) each has diameter ≤2a_i≤2r, by the maximum formula for distances. There are countably many blocks, and N001 permits reindexing them by ℕ with empty padding.

produces.statement: blocks is a countable cover of A×I with diam(blocks_{i,j})≤2a_i≤2r, and 1≤N_i≤2/a_i for every i.

argument.text:
By F004, q+1>0 and the nonnegative real-power laws,
∑_i∑_{j<N_i} diam(blocks_{i,j})^(q+1)
 ≤∑_i N_i(2a_i)^(q+1)
 ≤2^(q+2)∑_i a_i^q
 <2^(q+2)ε.
The second inequality follows termwise from N_i≤2/a_i and a_i>0, since (2/a_i)(2a_i)^(q+1)=2^(q+2)a_i^q. Empty original indices have K_i=∅ and cost zero. All inequalities of infinite nonnegative sums follow from finite subsums, so remain valid without a preliminary summability assumption. This gives the quantitative cover for the arbitrary r,ε. Discharge L2 and universally quantify them; the resulting quantitative statement is F005.

produces.statement: For every real r0,ε0 with 0<r0≤1 and ε0>0, A×I in maxProd(X,ℝ) has a countable 2r0-cover of (q+1)-cost <2^(q+2)ε0. The constant depends only on q.

argument.text: For any positive target scale Δ and tolerance τ, set rTarget=min(1,Δ/2)>0 and εTarget=τ/(2·2^(q+2))>0. F005 gives a cover of diameter ≤2rTarget≤Δ and cost <2^(q+2)εTarget=τ/2<τ. N001, now in maxProd(X,ℝ) with its Borel structure and positive exponent q+1, yields μH[q+1](A×I)=0. This and F005 are the two clauses of the asserted output. Discharge L1 and quantify X,A,q; Δ,τ were arbitrary small-cover test values, not new hypotheses.

definitions.type: extended diameter, for subsets of a pseudo extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a pseudo extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y): x∈B, y∈B} in [0,∞], with sup ∅=0.

definitions.type: real diameter notation for subsets of a metric space
definitions.definition: For a metric space Z and B⊆Z, diam(B)=(ediam(B)).toReal, where toReal agrees with finite nonnegative reals and sends ∞ to 0. Only finite-extended-diameter sets are assigned real diameters in our covering arguments. Empty sets and singletons have diameter zero.

definitions.type: extended nonnegative content C_p(r,B), also denoted YuiContent p r B
definitions.definition: For a metric (or extended metric) space Z, real p, r∈[0,∞], B⊆Z, define C_p(r,B)=inf_{U:ℕ→Set Z} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} ∑_{i≥0} sup_{h:U_i≠∅}(ediam(U_i))^p. Empty infima are ∞ and empty suprema are 0. Thus empty cover members cost zero, also at p=0. This is exactly YuiContent in basis-registry.json/lean_header. For a real scale δ≥0, C_p(δ,B) means C_p(ofReal δ,B); nonnegative real finite costs are embedded in [0,∞].

definitions.type: unnormalized diameter-power Hausdorff measure μH[p] on Borel extended metric spaces
definitions.definition: μH[p] is the native unnormalized Hausdorff measure, MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure p = Measure.mkMetric (r↦r^p). Its underlying outer measure is obtained from the metric outer measure construction: at each positive scale infimize the sums of diameter powers of countable covers, empty members costing zero, then take the supremum as the scale tends to zero. Evaluation μH[p](B) is the outer-measure value on any B⊆Z, with no measurability assumption on B. Explicitly, μH[p](B)=sup_{r∈[0,∞],r>0} C_p(r,B), including all extended positive scales.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.definition: For metric spaces Z,Y, maxProd(Z,Y) is Z×Y with distance between (x,t),(y,u) equal to max(dist_Z(x,y),dist_Y(t,u)). For real normed spaces this is the standard max norm on the product. Products in auxiliary propositions use this metric unless explicitly Euclidean.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on ℝ, with its Borel measurable structure
definitions.definition: volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, whose values on arbitrary subsets mean its outer-measure values. For a measurable space Z, measure ν and B⊆Z, ν|B denotes the restricted measure; on measurable S it has value ν(S∩B).
For B⊆Z, indicator(B)(t)=1 when t∈B and 0 otherwise; w indicator(B) is the function equal to w on B and 0 off B, for w∈[0,∞], including w=∞.

For a measure ν on a measurable space Z and f:Z→[0,∞], lintegral_ν(f)=∫⁻ f dν is the supremum of integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions bounded pointwise by f. The integral of a simple function is the finite sum of its distinct nonzero values times the measure of the corresponding fibers. ∫⁻_B f dν means lintegral_{ν|B}(f).

inputs.statement: For every metric space X with its Borel structure, A⊆X and real p>0, at each finite positive real scale δ, C_p(δ,A) is exactly the infimum of ∑_i diam(U_i)^p over countable δ-covers of A, with empty members costing zero. Each cover bounds content above. It is antitone in δ; μH[p](A)=sup_{δ∈ℝ,δ>0} C_p(δ,A). Moreover μH[p](A)=0 iff for every δ>0 and ε>0 an admissible ℕ-indexed cover has cost <ε. Suprema along scales decreasing to zero give the same measure. These agree exactly with the original H^p_δ and H^p, without a normalization factor. Countable subfamilies and pairs (i,j) with j<N_i may be enumerated by ℕ and padded by empty sets without changing coverage or nonnegative cost.
For pseudo extended metric spaces Z,Y, a nonnegative real K, and a map f:Z→Y satisfying edist(f(x),f(y))≤K edist(x,y) for every x,y∈Z, every B⊆Z satisfies ediam(f '' B)≤K ediam(B).

K is a nonnegative real.
f is K-Lipschitz in extended distance.

source_conditions: Z is a measurable space and ν is a measure on it.
f≤g pointwise.

output.statement: For every metric space X with its Borel structure, A⊆X, real s>0 and finite real δ>0, C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I) in maxProd(X,ℝ); consequently μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I). These inequalities hold in [0,∞] even when C_s(δ,A)=∞ and without any measurability, compactness or nonemptiness assumption on A or the cover members.

locals.type: metric space with its Borel structure
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X with its Borel structure.
Fix any subset A⊆X.
Fix a real exponent s.
Fix a real finite scale δ and temporarily assume L1: s>0 and δ>0.
Fix any family U; temporarily assume L2: U covers A×I and each ediam(U_i)≤δ.
Set cost=∑_i diam(U_i)^(s+1), with empty summands zero.
Set c=C_s(δ,A), without a finiteness assumption.
Set px(x,t)=x.
Set pt(x,t)=t.
Set ρ_i=diam(U_i), equal to zero when U_i is empty.
Set Ax_i=px '' U_i.
Set Bt_i=pt '' U_i.
Fix arbitrary ε under L3: ε>0.
For nonempty U_i set J_i=(inf Bt_i−η_i/2,sup Bt_i+η_i/2); for empty U_i set J_i=∅.
Set Ws_i(t)=Ax_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise.
Set g_i(t)=ρ_i^s indicator(J_i∩I)(t).

argument.text: Fix X,A,s,δ and temporarily assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Put the product A×I in maxProd(X,ℝ). Fix an arbitrary ℕ-indexed family U under L2: it covers A×I and ediam(U_i)≤δ for every i. Let cost=∑_i diam(U_i)^(s+1), with empty terms zero, and c=C_s(δ,A). The cover diameters are finite, but c and cost may be infinite. Define px(x,t)=x and pt(x,t)=t. The distance in either coordinate is at most the maximum of the two coordinate distances, so both projections are 1-Lipschitz in extended distance.

produces.statement: Both coordinate projections px and pt are 1-Lipschitz for the max product.

argument.text: Define ρ_i=diam(U_i), Ax_i=px '' U_i and Bt_i=pt '' U_i. Applying M016 to each projection, justified by F001, gives ediam(Ax_i)≤ediam(U_i) and ediam(Bt_i)≤ediam(U_i); thus diam(Ax_i),diam(Bt_i)≤ρ_i≤δ. Empty U_i gives empty projections and ρ_i=0. For any nonempty index the set Bt_i is nonempty and bounded: a point b₀∈Bt_i exists, and |b−b₀|≤ρ_i for every b∈Bt_i. Its real infimum and supremum therefore bound all its points. Taking suprema in b−b'≤ρ_i gives sup Bt_i−inf Bt_i≤ρ_i. This uses only completeness of ℝ for nonempty bounded sets, not measurability of a projection.

produces.statement: For every i, 0≤ρ_i≤δ and ediam(Ax_i),ediam(Bt_i)≤ofReal ρ_i. For nonempty U_i, Bt_i is nonempty and bounded with all its points between inf Bt_i and sup Bt_i and sup Bt_i−inf Bt_i≤ρ_i; for empty U_i both projections are empty and ρ_i=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary ε under L3: ε>0, and define η_i=ε·2^(−i−1)/(1+ρ_i^s)>0. For a nonempty U_i define J_i=(inf Bt_i−η_i/2,sup Bt_i+η_i/2); for an empty U_i define J_i=∅. F002 shows Bt_i⊆J_i, including when Bt_i is a singleton, and the interval's length is at most ρ_i+η_i. These intervals and ∅ are Borel sets. No U_i or projection is required to be measurable.

produces.statement: For every i, J_i is Borel, Bt_i⊆J_i and, if U_i is nonempty, the open interval J_i has length at most ρ_i+η_i; if U_i is empty, J_i=∅. Each η_i is positive.

argument.text: For each t∈I define Ws_i(t)=Ax_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise. For every x∈A the covering property supplies an index i with (x,t)∈U_i, whence x∈Ax_i and t∈Bt_i⊆J_i. Thus this is a δ-cover of A. Its s-cost is ≤∑_iρ_i^s indicator(J_i)(t), using F002 and s>0 also at zero diameters. N001 therefore gives c≤∑_iρ_i^s indicator(J_i)(t) for t∈I. Define the zero-extended summands g_i(t)=ρ_i^s indicator(J_i∩I)(t). Then c indicator(I)(t)≤∑_i g_i(t) for all real t: the preceding inequality holds on I and both sides vanish off I. Each g_i is measurable, since J_i∩I is Borel and its finite weight ρ_i^s is constant.

produces.statement: For every t∈ℝ, c indicator(I)(t)≤∑_i g_i(t), where g_i(t)=ρ_i^s indicator(J_i∩I)(t); each g_i is Borel measurable and c=C_s(δ,A).

argument.text:
We may compute the integral over I or equivalently the integral of the zero extension over ℝ. M014 with endpoints 0,1 gives volume(I)=1. M013 with ν=volume, set I and constant c gives ∫⁻_I c dvolume=c·1=c even for c=∞. M011 for the measurable set I computes the integral of c indicator(I) to the same value. Apply M012 to the pointwise inequality F004, M010 to the ℕ-indexed measurable functions g_i, and M011 to each Borel set J_i∩I with constant ρ_i^s. We obtain
 c≤∫⁻ (∑_i g_i) dvolume
   =∑_i ∫⁻ g_i dvolume
   =∑_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I).
Every use is a nonnegative integral, so no finite-integral or absolute-summability condition is imposed.

produces.statement: c≤∑_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I), with c possibly ∞.

argument.text:
By measure monotonicity volume(J_i∩I)≤volume(J_i). For each nonempty index M015 gives volume(J_i)=ofReal(sup Bt_i−inf Bt_i+η_i)≤ofReal(ρ_i+η_i), using F003; at empty indices volume(J_i)=0. Thus
 c≤∑_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I)
  ≤∑_i ρ_i^s(ρ_i+η_i)
  =∑_iρ_i^(s+1)+∑_iη_iρ_i^s
  ≤cost+ε.
Here the power identity also holds at ρ_i=0 since s>0. The error is termwise bounded by ε·2^(−i−1), since η_iρ_i^s=ε·2^(−i−1)ρ_i^s/(1+ρ_i^s)≤ε·2^(−i−1). Its sum is ≤ε, because ∑_{i≥0}2^(−i−1)=1, as follows from finite geometric sums and their increasing limit. Splitting and comparing nonnegative sums is justified by taking suprema of finite subsums, including infinite totals. The first main sum is cost by its definition. Discharge L3 and quantify the arbitrary ε to get F006.

produces.statement: For every ε0>0, c≤cost+ε0 in [0,∞].

argument.text: F006 implies c≤cost. If cost=∞ this is immediate. If cost<∞ but c>cost, order density permits a finite positive ε with cost+ε<c (also when c=∞), contradicting F006. This argument needs no finiteness of c. Since U was arbitrary, discharge L2 and quantify U: every admissible δ-cover of A×I has (s+1)-cost at least C_s(δ,A).

produces.statement: Every ℕ-indexed δ-cover Vcover of A×I in maxProd(X,ℝ) satisfies C_s(δ,A)≤∑_i diam(Vcover_i)^(s+1), with empty terms zero.

argument.text: Infimizing the bound F007 over the admissible families gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I), using the ordinary-cost identification N001. If there is no admissible family the right side is ∞ and the same inequality holds. Thus the bound holds for every finite δ>0; take suprema over these scales and apply N001 at the positive exponents s and s+1 to obtain μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I). Discharge L1 and quantify the arbitrary X,A,s,δ. This proves both clauses of the asserted output, without adding any measurability or compactness premise.

locals.declaration: Fix any finite dimensional real normed space V.
Fix A⊆V and temporarily assume L1: A is nonempty and compact.
Set d=(dimH(A)).toReal.
Set h=dimH(A×I) in maxProd(V,ℝ).
Fix arbitrary real q under L2: q>d.
Set hreal=h.toReal; finiteness of h is first proved in S004.
Under the contradiction branch L3 set qUpper=(d+hreal−1)/2.
Under L4: d>0, fix arbitrary real s under L5: 0<s<d.

argument.text: Fix V,A and assume L1: A is nonempty compact. Put d=(dimH(A)).toReal and h=dimH(A×I) in the max product. N004 gives dimH(A)≤finrank(V)<∞; hence d≥0 and dimH(A) is exactly the finite nonnegative-real embedding of d. Nonemptiness in L1 also gives existence of a point of A. We retain compactness in the conditional theorem, although the following dimension argument only needs the finite ambient bound and nonemptiness.

produces.statement: d≥0, dimH(A)=ofReal d<∞, and there exists x0∈A.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary real q under L2: q>d. By F001, q>0 and dimH(A)<q. Equip V with its Borel structure and regard q as a nonnegative real, without changing its real exponent. M003 gives μH[q](A)=0.

produces.statement: q>0 and μH[q](A)=0.

argument.text: N002 at X=V, exponent q and set A gives μH[q+1](A×I)=0. Since 0≠∞, M004 applied in maxProd(V,ℝ), at nonnegative exponent q+1, gives h≤q+1. Discharge L2 and quantify q: this bound holds for every q>d.

produces.statement: For every real q0>d, h≤ofReal(q0+1).

argument.text: F003 with q=d+1 gives h≤d+2<∞. Set hreal=h.toReal, so h=ofReal hreal and hreal≥0. Temporarily assume L3: hreal>d+1. The real number qUpper=(d+hreal−1)/2 lies strictly between d and hreal−1. F003 would give hreal≤qUpper+1<hreal, a contradiction. Discharge L3, obtaining hreal≤d+1 and thus h≤ofReal(d+1). This is the limiting upper bound, using no subtraction of infinite extended numbers.

produces.statement: h<∞, h=ofReal hreal, hreal≥0 and hreal≤d+1.

argument.text: First take the branch L4: d>0. Fix arbitrary real s under L5: 0<s<d. In V with its Borel structure, F001 gives s<dimH(A); regard s as a nonnegative real. M002 gives μH[s](A)=∞.

produces.statement: s>0 and μH[s](A)=∞.

argument.text: N003 at X=V, set A and exponent s gives μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I); hence the latter measure is ∞ by F005. M005 at exponent s+1 in maxProd(V,ℝ) gives s+1≤h. Discharge L5 and universally quantify s to record the full family of lower bounds.

produces.statement: For every real s0 with 0<s0<d, ofReal(s0+1)≤h.

argument.text: Under L4, suppose temporarily L6: hreal<d+1. Since d>0, max(0,hreal−1)<d. Put sLower=(max(0,hreal−1)+d)/2. Then 0<sLower<d and sLower+1>hreal, contradicting F006 and the finite identification in F004. Discharge L6 to obtain d+1≤hreal. Discharge L4 into the implication: if d>0 then ofReal(d+1)≤h. This is the lower limiting step.

produces.statement: If d>0 then ofReal(d+1)≤h.

argument.text: For the other branch assume L7: d=0. By the existence assertion in F001 choose x0∈A. Define j:ℝ→maxProd(V,ℝ) by j(t)=(x0,t). For all real t,u the product distance is max(dist_V(x0,x0),|t−u|)=|t−u|, so j is an isometry. Since x0∈A, j '' I⊆A×I.

produces.statement: j is an isometry from ℝ to maxProd(V,ℝ), and j '' I⊆A×I.

argument.text: M007 applied to j gives dimH(j '' I)=dimH(I). N005 is dimH(I)=1. M006 applied to the inclusion F008 gives dimH(j '' I)≤dimH(A×I)=h. Thus 1≤h; since d=0, ofReal(d+1)≤h. Discharge L7 into that implication. The identity of the private x0 is immaterial to the exported inequality.

produces.statement: If d=0 then ofReal(d+1)≤h.

argument.text: By F001, d≥0, so either d>0 or d=0. F007 and F009 give ofReal(d+1)≤h in the respective exhaustive branches. F004 gives the reverse inequality, and F001 identifies dimH(A) with d. Thus dimH(A×I)=dimH(A)+1. If finrank(V)=0 then N004 gives d=0 and the same zero branch applies; no positive-dimensional ball was needed in the upper-cover or slicing arguments. Discharge L1 and quantify V,A to prove the asserted output with precisely its stated nonempty compact premise.

Fix any subset A⊆X.
Fix a real exponent s.
Fix a real finite scale δ and temporarily assume L1: s>0 and δ>0.
Fix any family U; temporarily assume L2: U covers A×I and each ediam(U_i)≤δ.
Set cost=∑_i diam(U_i)^(s+1), with empty summands zero.
Set c=C_s(δ,A), without a finiteness assumption.
Set px(x,t)=x.
Set pt(x,t)=t.
Set ρ_i=diam(U_i), equal to zero when U_i is empty.
Set Ax_i=px '' U_i.
Set Bt_i=pt '' U_i.
Fix arbitrary ε under L3: ε>0.
For nonempty U_i set J_i=(inf Bt_i−η_i/2,sup Bt_i+η_i/2); for empty U_i set J_i=∅.
Set Ws_i(t)=Ax_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise.
Set g_i(t)=ρ_i^s indicator(J_i∩I)(t).

argument.text: Fix X,A,s,δ and temporarily assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Put the product A×I in maxProd(X,ℝ). Fix an arbitrary ℕ-indexed family U under L2: it covers A×I and ediam(U_i)≤δ for every i. Let cost=∑_i diam(U_i)^(s+1), with empty terms zero, and c=C_s(δ,A). The cover diameters are finite, but c and cost may be infinite. Define px(x,t)=x and pt(x,t)=t. The distance in either coordinate is at most the maximum of the two coordinate distances, so both projections are 1-Lipschitz in extended distance.

produces.statement: Both coordinate projections px and pt are 1-Lipschitz for the max product.

argument.text: Define ρ_i=diam(U_i), Ax_i=px '' U_i and Bt_i=pt '' U_i. Applying M016 to each projection, justified by F001, gives ediam(Ax_i)≤ediam(U_i) and ediam(Bt_i)≤ediam(U_i); thus diam(Ax_i),diam(Bt_i)≤ρ_i≤δ. Empty U_i gives empty projections and ρ_i=0. For any nonempty index the set Bt_i is nonempty and bounded: a point b₀∈Bt_i exists, and |b−b₀|≤ρ_i for every b∈Bt_i. Its real infimum and supremum therefore bound all its points. Taking suprema in b−b'≤ρ_i gives sup Bt_i−inf Bt_i≤ρ_i. This uses only completeness of ℝ for nonempty bounded sets, not measurability of a projection.

produces.statement: For every i, 0≤ρ_i≤δ and ediam(Ax_i),ediam(Bt_i)≤ofReal ρ_i. For nonempty U_i, Bt_i is nonempty and bounded with all its points between inf Bt_i and sup Bt_i and sup Bt_i−inf Bt_i≤ρ_i; for empty U_i both projections are empty and ρ_i=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary ε under L3: ε>0, and define η_i=ε·2^(−i−1)/(1+ρ_i^s)>0. For a nonempty U_i define J_i=(inf Bt_i−η_i/2,sup Bt_i+η_i/2); for an empty U_i define J_i=∅. F002 shows Bt_i⊆J_i, including when Bt_i is a singleton, and the interval's length is at most ρ_i+η_i. These intervals and ∅ are Borel sets. No U_i or projection is required to be measurable.

produces.statement: For every i, J_i is Borel, Bt_i⊆J_i and, if U_i is nonempty, the open interval J_i has length at most ρ_i+η_i; if U_i is empty, J_i=∅. Each η_i is positive.

argument.text: For each t∈I define Ws_i(t)=Ax_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise. For every x∈A the covering property supplies an index i with (x,t)∈U_i, whence x∈Ax_i and t∈Bt_i⊆J_i. Thus this is a δ-cover of A. Its s-cost is ≤∑_iρ_i^s indicator(J_i)(t), using F002 and s>0 also at zero diameters. N001 therefore gives c≤∑_iρ_i^s indicator(J_i)(t) for t∈I. Define the zero-extended summands g_i(t)=ρ_i^s indicator(J_i∩I)(t). Then c indicator(I)(t)≤∑_i g_i(t) for all real t: the preceding inequality holds on I and both sides vanish off I. Each g_i is measurable, since J_i∩I is Borel and its finite weight ρ_i^s is constant.

produces.statement: For every t∈ℝ, c indicator(I)(t)≤∑_i g_i(t), where g_i(t)=ρ_i^s indicator(J_i∩I)(t); each g_i is Borel measurable and c=C_s(δ,A).

argument.text:
We may compute the integral over I or equivalently the integral of the zero extension over ℝ. M014 with endpoints 0,1 gives volume(I)=1. M013 with ν=volume, set I and constant c gives ∫⁻_I c dvolume=c·1=c even for c=∞. M011 for the measurable set I computes the integral of c indicator(I) to the same value. Apply M012 to the pointwise inequality F004, M010 to the ℕ-indexed measurable functions g_i, and M011 to each Borel set J_i∩I with constant ρ_i^s. We obtain
 c≤∫⁻ (∑_i g_i) dvolume
   =∑_i ∫⁻ g_i dvolume
   =∑_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I).
Every use is a nonnegative integral, so no finite-integral or absolute-summability condition is imposed.

produces.statement: c≤∑_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I), with c possibly ∞.

argument.text:
By measure monotonicity volume(J_i∩I)≤volume(J_i). For each nonempty index M015 gives volume(J_i)=ofReal(sup Bt_i−inf Bt_i+η_i)≤ofReal(ρ_i+η_i), using F003; at empty indices volume(J_i)=0. Thus
 c≤∑_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I)
  ≤∑_i ρ_i^s(ρ_i+η_i)
  =∑_iρ_i^(s+1)+∑_iη_iρ_i^s
  ≤cost+ε.
Here the power identity also holds at ρ_i=0 since s>0. The error is termwise bounded by ε·2^(−i−1), since η_iρ_i^s=ε·2^(−i−1)ρ_i^s/(1+ρ_i^s)≤ε·2^(−i−1). Its sum is ≤ε, because ∑_{i≥0}2^(−i−1)=1, as follows from finite geometric sums and their increasing limit. Splitting and comparing nonnegative sums is justified by taking suprema of finite subsums, including infinite totals. The first main sum is cost by its definition. Discharge L3 and quantify the arbitrary ε to get F006.

argument.text: F006 implies c≤cost. If cost=∞ this is immediate. If cost<∞ but c>cost, order density permits a finite positive ε with cost+ε<c (also when c=∞), contradicting F006. This argument needs no finiteness of c. Since U was arbitrary, discharge L2 and quantify U: every admissible δ-cover of A×I has (s+1)-cost at least C_s(δ,A).

argument.text: Infimizing the bound F007 over the admissible families gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I), using the ordinary-cost identification N001. If there is no admissible family the right side is ∞ and the same inequality holds. Thus the bound holds for every finite δ>0; take suprema over these scales and apply N001 at the positive exponents s and s+1 to obtain μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I). Discharge L1 and quantify the arbitrary X,A,s,δ. This proves both clauses of the asserted output, without adding any measurability or compactness premise.

argument.text: For the forward small-cover assertion temporarily suppose L2: μH[p](A)=0. By F002, every finite-scale content is zero. At a fixed positive δ and ε, if no admissible cost were <ε then every admissible cost would be ≥ε and its infimum would be ≥ε; if there were no admissible family the infimum would be ∞. Both contradict zero content. Thus there is a cover of cost <ε for every δ>0, ε>0. Discharge L2 into this implication. Conversely temporarily suppose L3: such covers exist for all δ>0 and ε>0. Each content is then ≤ε for every ε>0, and is nonnegative, so is zero by order density in [0,∞]. F002 gives μH[p](A)=0. Discharge L3. This establishes both directions without assuming a minimizer of an infimum.

argument.text: At finite scale every nonempty cover member has finite ediam, equal to the embedding of its real diam. Thus the infimum in D004 is precisely the original ordinary-diameter infimum H^p_δ, and F002 identifies μH[p] with the original H^p with no factor. Inject it into ℕ, place each set at its assigned index, and use ∅ elsewhere. The union is unchanged and each nonzero cost occurs once; the sum, defined as the supremum of finite subsums, is unchanged. These conclusions, F002 and F003 hold for all the arbitrary objects. Discharge L1 into p>0 and universally quantify to obtain every clause of the asserted output.

locals.declaration: Fix any finite dimensional real normed space V.
Fix A⊆V and temporarily assume L1: A is nonempty and compact.
Set d=(dimH(A)).toReal.
Set h=dimH(A×I) in maxProd(V,ℝ).
Fix arbitrary real q under L2: q>d.
Set hreal=h.toReal; finiteness of h is first proved in S004.
Under the contradiction branch L3 set qUpper=(d+hreal−1)/2.
Under L4: d>0, fix arbitrary real s under L5: 0<s<d.

argument.text: Fix V,A and assume L1: A is nonempty compact. Put d=(dimH(A)).toReal and h=dimH(A×I) in the max product. N004 gives dimH(A)≤finrank(V)<∞; hence d≥0 and dimH(A) is exactly the finite nonnegative-real embedding of d. Nonemptiness in L1 also gives existence of a point of A. We retain compactness in the conditional theorem, although the following dimension argument only needs the finite ambient bound and nonemptiness.

produces.statement: d≥0, dimH(A)=ofReal d<∞, and there exists x0∈A.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary real q under L2: q>d. By F001, q>0 and dimH(A)<q. Equip V with its Borel structure and regard q as a nonnegative real, without changing its real exponent. M003 gives μH[q](A)=0.

produces.statement: q>0 and μH[q](A)=0.

argument.text: N002 at X=V, exponent q and set A gives μH[q+1](A×I)=0. Since 0≠∞, M004 applied in maxProd(V,ℝ), at nonnegative exponent q+1, gives h≤q+1. Discharge L2 and quantify q: this bound holds for every q>d.

produces.statement: For every real q0>d, h≤ofReal(q0+1).

argument.text: F003 with q=d+1 gives h≤d+2<∞. Set hreal=h.toReal, so h=ofReal hreal and hreal≥0. Temporarily assume L3: hreal>d+1. The real number qUpper=(d+hreal−1)/2 lies strictly between d and hreal−1. F003 would give hreal≤qUpper+1<hreal, a contradiction. Discharge L3, obtaining hreal≤d+1 and thus h≤ofReal(d+1). This is the limiting upper bound, using no subtraction of infinite extended numbers.

produces.statement: h<∞, h=ofReal hreal, hreal≥0 and hreal≤d+1.

argument.text: First take the branch L4: d>0. Fix arbitrary real s under L5: 0<s<d. In V with its Borel structure, F001 gives s<dimH(A); regard s as a nonnegative real. M002 gives μH[s](A)=∞.

produces.statement: s>0 and μH[s](A)=∞.

argument.text: N003 at X=V, set A and exponent s gives μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I); hence the latter measure is ∞ by F005. M005 at exponent s+1 in maxProd(V,ℝ) gives s+1≤h. Discharge L5 and universally quantify s to record the full family of lower bounds.

produces.statement: For every real s0 with 0<s0<d, ofReal(s0+1)≤h.

argument.text: Under L4, suppose temporarily L6: hreal<d+1. Since d>0, max(0,hreal−1)<d. Put sLower=(max(0,hreal−1)+d)/2. Then 0<sLower<d and sLower+1>hreal, contradicting F006 and the finite identification in F004. Discharge L6 to obtain d+1≤hreal. Discharge L4 into the implication: if d>0 then ofReal(d+1)≤h. This is the lower limiting step.

produces.statement: If d>0 then ofReal(d+1)≤h.

argument.text: For the other branch assume L7: d=0. By the existence assertion in F001 choose x0∈A. Define j:ℝ→maxProd(V,ℝ) by j(t)=(x0,t). For all real t,u the product distance is max(dist_V(x0,x0),|t−u|)=|t−u|, so j is an isometry. Since x0∈A, j '' I⊆A×I.

produces.statement: j is an isometry from ℝ to maxProd(V,ℝ), and j '' I⊆A×I.

argument.text: M007 applied to j gives dimH(j '' I)=dimH(I). N005 is dimH(I)=1. M006 applied to the inclusion F008 gives dimH(j '' I)≤dimH(A×I)=h. Thus 1≤h; since d=0, ofReal(d+1)≤h. Discharge L7 into that implication. The identity of the private x0 is immaterial to the exported inequality.

produces.statement: If d=0 then ofReal(d+1)≤h.

argument.text: By F001, d≥0, so either d>0 or d=0. F007 and F009 give ofReal(d+1)≤h in the respective exhaustive branches. F004 gives the reverse inequality, and F001 identifies dimH(A) with d. Thus dimH(A×I)=dimH(A)+1. If finrank(V)=0 then N004 gives d=0 and the same zero branch applies; no positive-dimensional ball was needed in the upper-cover or slicing arguments. Discharge L1 and quantify V,A to prove the asserted output with precisely its stated nonempty compact premise.

Coordinate expansion gives spanning and comparison of each coordinate gives independence. Thus both maxProd(Vn,ℝ) and Wn are finite dimensional real normed spaces, using the standard max norm on the former. definitions.type: extended diameter, for subsets of a pseudo extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a pseudo extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y): x∈B, y∈B} in [0,∞], with sup ∅=0.

definitions.type: extended nonnegative content C_p(r,B), also denoted YuiContent p r B
definitions.definition: For a metric (or extended metric) space Z, real p, r∈[0,∞], B⊆Z, define C_p(r,B)=inf_{U:ℕ→Set Z} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} ∑_{i≥0} sup_{h:U_i≠∅}(ediam(U_i))^p. Empty infima are ∞ and empty suprema are 0. Thus empty cover members cost zero, also at p=0. This is exactly YuiContent in basis-registry.json/lean_header. For a real scale δ≥0, C_p(δ,B) means C_p(ofReal δ,B); nonnegative real finite costs are embedded in [0,∞]. Throughout, a δ-cover means a family covering the set with ediam of every member ≤ofReal δ; the finite-scale real-diameter notation never admits an unbounded member through toReal(∞)=0.

definitions.type: unnormalized diameter-power Hausdorff measure μH[p] on Borel extended metric spaces
definitions.definition: μH[p] is the native unnormalized Hausdorff measure, MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure p = Measure.mkMetric (r↦r^p). Its underlying outer measure is obtained from the metric outer measure construction: at each positive scale infimize the sums of diameter powers of countable covers, empty members costing zero, then take the supremum as the scale tends to zero. Evaluation μH[p](B) is the outer-measure value on any B⊆Z, with no measurability assumption on B. Explicitly, μH[p](B)=sup_{r∈[0,∞],r>0} C_p(r,B), including all extended positive scales.

binders.type: extended metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.definition: For an extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, dimH(B)=sup{a∈[0,∞): μH[a](B)=∞}, evaluated in [0,∞] using the Borel measurable structure. The supremum of an empty set of exponents is 0. This is the native Hausdorff dimension with the original critical-exponent convention; the equality of the native measure and the original positive-exponent covering normalization is established in the proof.

For metric spaces Z,Y, maxProd(Z,Y) is Z×Y with distance between (x,t),(y,u) equal to max(dist_Z(x,y),dist_Y(t,u)). For real normed spaces this is the standard max norm on the product. Products in auxiliary propositions use this metric unless explicitly Euclidean.
For a finite dimensional real vector space Z, finrank(Z)=Module.finrank ℝ Z is the natural-number cardinality of any finite basis. Natural values are embedded into [0,∞] in dimension inequalities.
Vn=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), identified with ℝ^n with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. Fin n={0,...,n−1}; for n=0 it is empty and Vn consists of the zero tuple.
Wn=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin(n+1)), with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure.

T(x,t) has coordinates T(x,t)(i.castSucc)=x(i) for i∈Fin n and T(x,t)(Fin.last n)=t, where i.castSucc retains the index i<n in Fin(n+1) and Fin.last n is its last index n. This defines a total map without presupposing linearity or invertibility.
Fmax=E×I in maxProd(Vn,ℝ).
Feuc={z∈Wn : (i↦z(i.castSucc))∈E and z(Fin.last n)∈I}. This is exactly the Euclidean product subset E×[0,1] in the original target.

The constants are independent of n,E and points, and all assertions include n=0.
